title: The period of PURPLE crying: when fussiness peaks
summary: Increased crying between about 2 weeks and 3–4 months is common and usually temporary.
whatsNormal:
PURPLE is an acronym describing normal increased crying in early infancy, not a disease.

• Peak of crying often around 6–8 weeks
• Evening fussiness is typical
• Baby may look like they are in pain but are otherwise healthy, feeding, and gaining weight
• Crying can start and stop without an obvious cause

Soothing helps but does not always stop crying immediately. It is OK to put baby down in a safe sleep space and take a short break if you feel overwhelmed, never shake a baby.
watchFor: Crying with fever, vomiting, or a bulging soft spot
High-pitched, weak, or moaning cry that is new and different
Not feeding, fewer wet diapers, or unusual sleepiness
Crying only on one side or with clear injury to an arm or leg
callDoctorIf: You think this is more than normal fussiness, trust your instinct and call
Signs of illness: fever under 3 months, green vomit, or breathing difficulty
You feel unable to cope or angry enough to harm baby, put baby in a safe crib and call your clinician, a crisis line, or a trusted person immediately
Possible shaken baby or head injury, emergency care
